earlier_milestones.finding: 15-minute retained-collapse candidates only; explicitly not proof of an instantaneous crash candle.
One valid 30-second observed sparse red candle for B5yWXR; opening and candle OHLC retained, but no exact observed-peak MC/timestamp retained.
One valid 30-second observed sparse red candle for 6Ldj, with compact candle fields and peak-to-start timing retained.
Eleven valid observed red-candle records, all PARTIAL_30S_COVERAGE/PARTIAL_EXIT_EVIDENCE; no complete-window event.

implementation.contract: Validates timestamp ordering/alignment, positive finite OHLC values and OHLC consistency before calculating (1 - close/open) * 100. It retains only compact derived event fields and explicit coverage status.
implementation.reuse_status: Reusable only as the existing 30-second observed-exit normalizer; it must retain its PARTIAL versus COMPLETE distinction and is not a DEV026 1-minute post-ATH detector.

normalization_correction.details: The original one-shot path used unavailable ProviderTransportOutcome body/headers attributes. The qualified correction reads payload/response_headers and accepts established timestamp/OHLC aliases, while failing closed on malformed or inconsistent candles.
normalization_correction.separate_invalid_signal: Byzantine MCAP low-field scale discontinuity made low-based >=85% drawdowns artificial. It does not invalidate these open-to-close calculations, which use positive finite open and close fields; low-based 85% conclusions remain excluded.

representative_joined_event.limitation: The individual candle and its ordering after the retained observed peak are established, but sparse returned buckets mean it is not a complete-window or population-level crash conclusion.

conclusion: Existing evidence proves one reusable, ordered observed-partial post-peak crash candle with a pre-crash value 1.1769x opening. It does not provide a complete-coverage post-ATH crash population or support clustering inference around opening MC.
